config.title: Build keyboard shortcut manager

intro.title: Build keyboard shortcut manager
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a keyboard shortcut manager that allows users to trigger specific actions by pressing key combinations. You will learn how to handle keyboard events in JavaScript to detect when keys are pressed. The core programming concepts involved include event listeners, conditional logic, and managing state for active shortcuts. This project will help you understand how to create interactive web applications that respond to user input efficiently.
intro.usecase: Keyboard shortcuts are essential productivity features in professional software where users perform repetitive tasks. Developers implement them in code editors like VS Code for commands (Ctrl+S to save), in design tools like Figma for quick actions (V for selection tool), and in data dashboards for filtering and navigation. Mastering keyboard shortcut management allows you to build more efficient interfaces where power users can work faster without reaching for the mouse.

objectives: Implement a function to capture and process keyboard events
Construct a data structure to store keyboard shortcut mappings
Bind keyboard event listeners to the document or specific elements
Manipulate the DOM to display active shortcut status
Initialize and update shortcut configurations dynamically
Integrate multiple shortcut combinations for different actions
Control event propagation and prevent default browser behavior

steps.title: Import required modules
steps.instruction: Import the necessary modules for the keyboard shortcut manager. You'll need to import React and the useState hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the React library and useState hook available for building the keyboard shortcut manager.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create main keyboard shortcut manager function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'keyboardShortcutManager' that returns an empty object for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure it returns an empty object {}.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';
// Create the keyboardShortcutManager function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'keyboardShortcutManager' is defined and returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The function 'keyboardShortcutManager' is defined and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named 'keyboardShortcutManager' and returns an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please create a function named 'keyboardShortcutManager' that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize shortcuts storage object
steps.instruction: Inside the keyboardShortcutManager function, create an empty object named shortcuts to store registered keyboard shortcuts.
steps.hint: You can declare a variable with const and assign an empty object {} to it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an empty object for storage
const items = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a shortcuts object ready to store keyboard shortcuts.
successCriteria: A variable named shortcuts is declared and initialized as an empty object inside the keyboardShortcutManager function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've declared a variable named shortcuts and assigned an empty object {} to it inside the function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The shortcuts object wasn't created correctly. Check that you declared it inside the keyboardShortcutManager function.

steps.title: Export the keyboard shortcut manager
steps.instruction: Export the keyboardShortcutManager function so it can be imported and used in other JavaScript files.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before the function declaration to make it available for import elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: The keyboardShortcutManager function is properly exported, making it available for import in other modules.
successCriteria: The keyboardShortcutManager function is exported using the export keyword.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct export syntax. The function needs to be exported so other files can import it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The keyboard shortcut manager isn't properly exported. Remember to use the export keyword to make the function available for import in other modules.
